---
title: "manhattan plot"
format: html
editor: visual
---

```{r}
library(qqman)
```

GWAS fabae BLINK

```{r}
png( filename = "Manhathan_BLINK_fabae.png", width = 2000, height = 1800, res = 300 )

# 2. Load your GAPIT results
gwas <- read.csv(
  "../../../../../results_with_hedin/GWAS outpout/fabae/GAPIT.Association.GWAS_Results.BLINK.emmean(Kansas).csv",
  sep = ",",
  header = TRUE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# 3. Handle zero p-values
gwas$P.value[gwas$P.value == 0] <- 1e-300

# 4. Make sure chromosome is numeric for qqman
gwas$Chr <- as.numeric(gwas$Chr)

# 5. Optional: Remove NAs
gwas <- na.omit(gwas)

# 6. Define custom labels (optional, for x-axis)
chr_labels <- c("1" = "chr1S", "2" = "chr1L", "3" = "chr2",
                "4" = "chr3", "5" = "chr4", "6" = "chr5", "7" = "chr6")

# 7. Manhattan plot
manhattan(
  gwas,
  chr = "Chr",
  bp = "Pos",
  p = "P.value",
  snp = "SNP",
  col = c("grey70", "grey40"),
  suggestiveline = FALSE,
  genomewideline = FALSE,   # do NOT draw the default red line
  ylim = c(0, -log10(5e-16)),
  cex = 0.5, 
  main = "Manhattan Plot A.fabae - BLINK (Kansas)",
  chrlabs = chr_labels  # this will replace 1,2,3,... with your labels
)

# 2. Add a grey genome-wide threshold line manually
abline(h = -log10(5e-8), col = "grey50", lwd = 1, lty = 1)

dev.off()
```

```{r}
png( filename = "Manhathan_MLMM_pisum.png", width = 2000, height = 1800, res = 300 )

# 2. Load your GAPIT results
gwas <- read.csv(
  "../../../../../results_with_hedin/GWAS outpout/pisum/GAPIT.Association.GWAS_Results.MLMM.emmean(NYC).csv",
  sep = ",",
  header = TRUE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# 3. Handle zero p-values
gwas$P.value[gwas$P.value == 0] <- 1e-300

levels_order <- c(
  "chr1S",
  "chr1L",
  "chr2",
  "chr3",
  "chr4",
  "chr5",
  "chr6"
)

gwas$Chr <- as.numeric(
  factor(gwas$Chr, levels = levels_order)
)
# 4. Make sure chromosome is numeric for qqman
gwas$Chr <- as.numeric(gwas$Chr)

# 5. Optional: Remove NAs
gwas <- na.omit(gwas)

# 6. Define custom labels (optional, for x-axis)
chr_labels <- c("1" = "chr1S", "2" = "chr1L", "3" = "chr2",
                "4" = "chr3", "5" = "chr4", "6" = "chr5", "7" = "chr6")

# 7. Manhattan plot
manhattan(
  gwas,
  chr = "Chr",
  bp = "Pos",
  p = "P.value",
  snp = "SNP",
  col = c("grey70", "grey40"),
  suggestiveline = FALSE,
  genomewideline = FALSE,   # do NOT draw the default red line
  ylim = c(0, -log10(5e-16)),
  cex = 0.5, 
  main = "Manhattan Plot A.pisum - MLMM (Kansas)",
  chrlabs = chr_labels  # this will replace 1,2,3,... with your labels
)

# 2. Add a grey genome-wide threshold line manually
abline(h = -log10(5e-8), col = "grey50", lwd = 1, lty = 1)
```
